meaning: One of the separate resources inside a computer (a half of a CPU core, a memory limit, a GPU engine, storage, network) that a workload can fill while the others sit partly idle.
A part saturates when what the work demands per second equals what the part can deliver, so the job goes no faster.
The part of a core that fetches instructions and decodes them.
The part of a core that executes the decoded instructions on its arithmetic units.
The rate at which memory can stream bytes to a core, in GB/s.
The time one fetch from memory takes, in nanoseconds; the limit when each address depends on the value fetched before.
GPU units that execute matrix multiply-and-accumulate instructions, the arithmetic of neural networks.
The integer and floating-point units of a GPU that run ordinary GPU code, such as batched physics.
The core processing unit of an NVIDIA GPU; a card has many, and SM activity is the fraction of time they had work.
GPU hardware that speeds up the search for which triangle a ray hits.
The fixed-function engine on a GPU that compresses frames into video.
The fixed-function engine on a GPU that turns video back into frames.
NVIDIA's fleet monitoring tool, which reports per-part GPU fields such as SM, tensor and memory activity.
In nvidia-smi, the percentage of time at least one GPU program was executing; it does not say how much of the card was used.
One program run on the GPU.
The EC2 network device for ordinary IP networking: it moves data.
The EC2 network device that bypasses the operating system so many machines can train as one.
The network disk of an EC2 instance, with a throughput ceiling set by the instance type.
The unit EC2 counts processor capacity in; on most sizes two vCPUs are one physical core.
The video codec LeRobot writes by default.
A small imitation-learning policy that predicts a chunk of future actions at once.
A policy built on a vision-language model that takes images and text and outputs robot actions.
A portable file format for trained networks.
NVIDIA's inference compiler, which turns a network into an engine tuned for one GPU type.
A compiled version of a network tuned for one GPU type, built on the target device.
The event counters built into a processor.
A model's own compact summary of a frame, as a vector of numbers.
The corrections to the weights that a training step computes; in multi-node training every node exchanges them at every step.
A job described by three properties (duration, coupling, interruptibility) that decide how its machine is bought and scheduled.
How long one unit of a job's work runs.
Whether a job's pieces must exchange data while running, so that one needs its neighbours at the same moment.
Whether a job can lose its machine and resume, losing no more than one unit of work.
A small program measured in place of the real one (a MuJoCo humanoid for the arm, matrix-vector products for a policy).
One kind of job the robot's loop hands to a computer, such as decoding video or stepping a simulation.
One of the six steps the arm's data passes through: collect, curate, simulate, train, evaluate, deploy.
NVIDIA's desk-side computer whose CPU and GPU share one memory; one of the two machines of our measurements.
NVIDIA's small robot computer; the other machine of our measurements.
A small benchmark task in simulation: balance a pole on a moving cart.
NVIDIA's toolkit for curating physical AI training data.
The service that queues jobs and starts machines for them: AWS Batch, AWS Parallel Computing Service, Amazon SageMaker HyperPod or Amazon EKS.
Vary a training image (a crop, a colour shift) so the policy sees more variety.
